- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to counteract pessimism.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to forecast peaks.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if 10+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent 5-day low.
- Sentiment shifts > 0.5 in 3–5 days often trigger lagged forecast errors; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.33) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean.
